transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you're aware, Line 6 is scheduled to produce 1,400 medical-device housings this week, but our normally approved resin R-17 is temporarily unavailable. We do have an alternate medical-grade resin, R-22, available for a controlled run on Line 6. Before I can issue the engineering authorization to proceed, I need to go through our routine change-control review. So I'd like to hear from each of you — quality, process engineering, regulatory affairs, and production planning — on any constraints or concerns you have regarding using R-22 for this controlled run. Let's start with quality.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I checked the customer's revised control plan this morning, and it specifies that an alternate-resin run requires dimensional and tensile testing on exactly 50 first-off housings, with all 50 passing before the run can be released, plus retention of exactly 10 samples. I also want to flag that the revised plan has not yet been attached to the change-control record.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share a critical process constraint. My process trial showed that R-22 must be dried at 80 degrees Celsius for exactly 4 hours and requires a 45-minute screw purge before molding. I recorded this in my engineering notebook but have not yet entered it into the production setup sheet, so it won't be visible to the operators unless we update that sheet as part of this authorization.
